recs.name: Unexpected Annoyance
recs.tag: Oftentimes, worries spring from little nooks and crannies.

lines.x: Mountain, some of the bounty hunters went your way! Quite a few of them, too!
Don't worry. I can handle this much.
Hmph, where did these guys come from? Rhodes Island, remember this! I'll be back for you, you motherf...
Unfortunately, this is as far as you go.
Don't you think you can take us all down just because you're big!
Lads, let's go!
Hmph.
Looks like there are quite a few bounty hunters over there. Let's go back Mountain up.
Eh, sure, but I'm not too worried about him.
I doubt these guys are any match for Mountain.
Huh, you think so? I mean, he looks pretty tough, but he's always so polite. He just doesn't seem like that kind of guy.
This is your first time on a mission with him, huh?
That's what I used to think too. I thought maybe he just looked strong.
But it didn't take long for me to realize I got the wrong idea about him. This new guy's something else.
I mean...
Mean what?
*Howls*!!!
Yeah...
What was that?
We'll talk about this later. Let's go around to his twelve and see if we can catch a few guys that slipped past him.
What a... monster...
I'm nothing compared to others.
Phew...
I suppose trying to take on this many without help is pushing myself a little too far.
Mountain, we caught a few of these shitheads that got away.
Much appreciated.
Whoa, look at them, all beaten to a pulp. Now I feel sorry for them...
And look at this tree, ripped apart right down the middle. Now I see why you said I shouldn't have worried.
Right?
My apologies. I'm not very accustomed to team operations yet. I should've contacted you to come assist me.
Oh, no harm done. You handled yourself pretty well.

I wouldn't say that. Our mission objective is to stop the bounty hunters from being a nuisance to the nearby villages. Had any one of them managed to escape, we would not have solved the issue at hand.
If it wasn't for you two, our mission would have been a failure.
Well, look at you. What a diligent fella.
I hope that isn't a problem.
No, far from it. It's been a long time since we've had a new guy as diligent as you.
Enough about that. Are you okay?
I'm fine. Only a few scratches here and there. They'll heal up in no time.
I'm not talking about your scratches. I'm talking about your digs.
My clothes?
Mountain, your outfit is all burned up. You're basically naked right now.
Oh, uh, my apologies. This is quite embarrassing.
I tend to lose sight of these issues while I'm in a fight.
Haha, no worries. The exact same thing happened last time, though. Are you sure you don't want a different uniform just for field ops?
It's a waste to have to keep replacing a formal getup like that after every mission.
I'm used to dressing formally. You have a point, however. I will consider it.
You want formal clothing that's suitable for combat... am I correct?
Yes, and naturally, if this is too unreasonable of a request, please don't trouble yourself.
Hmm... First, I'm sure someone has already told you, but your uniforms need a special application.
Right. My Logistics operator told me that because there is no standard uniform suitable for my size, I'll need to apply for one.
At the time, I did not expect that I'd find myself in so many battles as an operator here, which is why I've never applied.
And your outfit's been getting torn into shreds after just a few missions.
Right.
Doesn't it get expensive when you need to keep paying for those fancy outfits?
To tell you the truth, I spent most of my first month's salary buying myself new clothes.
Huh? No way!
I'd just broken out of... Ahem, just left home. The equipment that Rhodes Island provides is more than adequate. There's not much I have to buy at my own expense, so this isn't a huge problem.
Nonetheless, I can imagine it turning into one sooner or later.
I guess you could probably just wear something else in combat... and that would solve most of the problem?
Indeed, and as I've already mentioned, I'm not actually adamant about wearing this.
However, I am rather fond of this style of attire. I've also noticed that the operators get rather personalized with the way they are dressed, so I thought I would ask if it would be possible.
If it isn't, then I will apply for a more durable combat uniform.
Hmm... Well, we don't get requests like this that often.
Our operators may have pretty unique wardrobes, but their outfits don't get in the way most of the time.
In that case, forget I asked.
Wait, I'm not done yet! I said we don't get these requests often, but I never said I'm turning you down.
Hm?
We need to put together a new outfit for you anyway. It'll take just a bit more work. It's okay.
Oh, right. This is perfect.
Orchid?
What now? I'm busy here. If you want to have tea, try somebody else.
Oh, that isn't what this is about, Orchid. Actually...
Please, Orchid?
This is giving me a headache already.
Oh, don't be like that. Look, you're always complaining about how boring it is to work in Logistics. This might just be a lot more fun than sitting in an office.
I basically run this place by myself. I'm exhausted.
There's a bonus in it.
No kidding?
Of course. You'll be helping solve our operators' problems.
That's a fairly nice motivator, and it almost worked, but I'm at most a designer, not a seamstress. If you need someone to work on clothes, I'm not the right person to ask.
Eh...
Hah... Fine, it just so happens I know who to ask.
Your codename is Mountain, correct?
Yes, ma'am.
Ma'am... No need for that. My codename is Orchid, and it'll do fine. Come with me.
Thank you very much, Orchid.
Be sure to save a slice of cake for me this afternoon.
Okay!
Orchid.
Hm?
About that conversation, is there a dedicated dressmaker at Rhodes Island?
No, I'm taking you to another operator here. She moonlights as a dressmaker.
Is that allowed?
What do you mean?
From my time here, I've always thought of Rhodes Island as something like a PMC.
I've never heard of a part-time dressmaker in these organizations.
You haven't spent much time at Rhodes Island yet, then.
What do you mean?
You have a grave misunderstanding about us here.
Okay, maybe it isn't really a misunderstanding. When I first came onboard, I felt more or less the same.
Care to elaborate?
The way you talk grates on my nerves just as much as Midnight, only in a different way...
Well, I could tell you, but you will know what I mean in a minute.

lines.st: Orchid stops in front of a dorm room and knocks on the door.

lines.x: Oh, good afternoon, Orchid.
Yes, hello.
May I ask who this is...?
I'm a new operator here, codename Mountain.
Oh, nice to meet you. I'm codename Bibeak.
Do you have any missions today?
Yes, but it isn't for another two hours.
Um, did you need me for something?
Two hours are plenty. Here's the thing...
Oh, I see. So Mountain wants formalwear that he can fight in!
If it's too much to ask for...
Not at all!
Actually, please let me work on it!
I need only to use fabrics suitable for combat... No, that isn't quite right. That would affect the beauty of the end product...
Bibeak, let's not stand here and talk about that. Give it a try.
Oh, yes!
I'm sorry. I haven't tried something like this before. It might take a while.
Not a problem. If this will lead somewhere, I am willing to give it some time.
Then please come with me.
What about you, Orchid? Will you come?
I still have a pile of documents to finish... as well as my cake... though I guess I could stay to take a look at the design.
I'm pretty curious how this outfit will turn out myself.
Is there something that makes you so insistent on wearing such formal attire?
No, I wouldn't say that.
Ever since I was a child, my father has made me dress in this particular manner, and I grew accustomed to it after a while.
Besides...
Oh, if you'd rather not talk about that, you don't have to. I'm just being curious.
No, not at all. I'm merely wondering whether I truly want to myself.
I've lived far away from my family for a very long period of time.
During that time, life has been... hard to say the least. I never had the opportunity to wear anything like this.
When I was finally able to leave that place behind and come to Rhodes Island, I bought myself a set of formalwear.
I can't say for certain whether this is partly because I miss my family... my parents.
I see... so you still can't see your parents, even now?
That's correct. One of the reasons I came to Rhodes Island is because I hope to be able to see them one day.
At the beginning of those difficult times, I very much missed my parents.
But as time went on, I also grew accustomed to life without them.
That is why I'm not certain whether this attire is something I choose to wear because I'm used to it or because I want it to serve as a reminder.
Why not both? That doesn't seem too odd.
You're right...
Speaking of which, are you a dressmaker, Bibeak?
Oh, I'm not. I just like to do some sewing on my off time.
It's been a while since I joined Rhodes Island, and many of our operators know about this hobby of mine, so they sometimes come to me for this.
And, Orchid, you mentioned being a designer yourself?
That's right. I used to be an editor at a fashion magazine.
Most of Rhodes Island's uniforms are mass-produced, but many of the folks here have got interesting personalities and want something different.
And that's when Bibeak and I shine.
*Sigh*... I used to do this pretty willingly, but, as time went on, I started to feel like we could just keep everyone in their uniforms if they all have to come to me with their weird requests.
Compared to all the other ones, this request is probably on the normal side.
But isn't it really fun to make clothes for others? Some of our requests may be a little weird, but it's actually pretty fun to make those designs come true.
Oh, my sweet child. Most everyone who says that ends up working themselves dead. Don't be so tolerant of others.
I think you're pretty tolerant of everyone in A6, though...
The moment she hears that, Orchid rolls her eyes.
You've been pretty quiet. Something the matter?
No. It's just your conversation has left me feeling like I'm taking a stroll down some busy street.
I'm thinking of introducing you to a certain Midnight later.
Is that an operator?
He is, and I'm looking forward to the conversations you two will have with each other.
Oh, there we go.
Is this... a storeroom?
Yes, this place is normally a storeroom, but I also use it to sew.
Now, Mountain, I'd like to take your measurements, if that is okay with you.
Okay.
Right, and that takes care of it.
By the way, do you have any preferences about your outfit's design?
Not at all. Something like what I'm wearing will do.
What about the color?
White will do.
Okay, then. Just leave the rest to me.
I'll come get you once it's ready.
Is that it?
Yes.
Even though you don't have any specific needs, we should probably work on a new design.
Oh, maybe I could modify the design I worked on last month!
The one you showed me?
Right.
Nothing wrong with that design, but I'm afraid it's far too refined for Mountain.
Hmm... You're right.
We're not in a rush with either designing or making the outfit, and the choice of the fabric is what's important.
I'll ask the Logistics operators in charge of uniforms. I'm sure they know what kind of fabrics are the right choice for combat suits.
I'll come with you.
Formalwear needs to be pleasing to the eye. I'm not sure the fabrics they normally use for combat uniforms are good enough aesthetically.
Well, I don't mind a little company, but isn't it about time for your mission?
Oh, shoot! I almost forgot!
I'm very sorry. Is it okay if we go together after I come back?
Of course, but you should report in for your mission.
Right!
Well, you heard her. Go home and wait. If Logistics get their hands on the right fabric, we should have something for you in a week.
Very well...
One week later...
Mountain, are you done yet?
One more second.
Here we go.
How does it feel?
Very comfortable.
I like the design, and the fabrics you used are very sturdy.
Much appreciated.
No, I should thank you.
The choice of fabric actually bothered me for a long time. I couldn't find anything that I'm satisfied with.
But then I remembered some of the fabrics that my father used when he worked on his industrial outfits.
I never thought of using those in my outfit designs, but I took the chance to give it a try, and it worked surprisingly well.
This has been an eye-opening experience.
I see. That's good to hear.
I suppose designers normally don't use industrial materials for their work... though Rhodes Island is not the place for common sense.
Well, then, I still have a mission, so please excuse me now.
If there are any problems with your outfit, feel free to come to me any time.
Of course.
Why are you standing there like an idiot?
No reason... It's just that when I see the two of you... it feels like I haven't fully grasped that I am free.
Thank you very much, Orchid.
No need to thank me for your uniform. I did what anyone should've done.
No, that's only part of it. You made me realize a few of the problems I still have.
I really wish it was Catapult or Midnight saying this to me instead of you.
I beg your pardon?
Nothing, just talking to myself. I don't know what you've been through, nor do I know what you came to Rhodes Island for.
There this one thing that a certain frivolous host asked me before. Maybe I should ask you the same question.
Please.
He asked me, 'What kind of life do you want to lead at Rhodes Island?'
Feel free to come to me if you need anything clothing-related.
Or rather, don't come to me. I'm a very busy woman. Try Bibeak if you need anything.
Okay.
Well... Perhaps I should really give some thought about my life here again.

recs.name: Sinner's Path
recs.tag: Though hesitant, one must still clench their fists and face the long, long walk ahead.

lines.x: Drip. Drop.
Is it raining?
He looks out the window. Lightning flashes across the sky, but the glass remains dry.
Tick, tock.
It must be the clock, then.
But he looks up at the clock, and sees that its hands have long since stopped, with only a broken wooden dummy swaying beneath.
What is going on?
His palm feels wet, as though liquid was dripping through his clenched fist and onto the ground, forming a viscous puddle.
He opens up his hand and sees that the hairs of his palm are soaked in blood.
Sinner.
Who's there?!
Hehe. You're already wearing unbreakable shackles, Anthony.

Another flash of lightning illuminates the corner of the dark room. A severed head lies on the ground, blood still gushing out from where it was separated from its body, leaving it lying in a pool of blood. It is the head that is speaking to him.
He remembers that face. It is a familiar one.
Val Hyde... where is your brother?
Where is he? Right by your feet.
He looks down to see a corpse lying on the ground. Its torso is turned away, yet its head has swiveled around to face him. The broken neck vertebrae protrude from the skin.
Why are you trembling, Anthony? You should be happy.
You've waited so long for this day. To kill your hated enemies with your own hands, and let their blood soak every inch of earth here.
Did... did I do all this?
Yes. Smile, Anthony. What a day. What a lovely day.
You've exacted your revenge, so why the long face? Hehehe.
No... it's too late.
Oh, my child, you came too late. Boo-hoo. Your mom and I didn't live to see the day you walked free again.
It's all too late. Our little Tony. Boo-hoo.
Shut up. Shut up!
Murderer! How dare you pretend to talk like my parents!
Murderer? Is he taking about us?
Yes, brother. He's talking about us.
But look around, Anthony. There's only one person in this room with blood on their hands.
It's you. You're the murderer.
You deserved it! You deserved to die by my hands!
Such brave words, such unwavering resolve. Everything is as you wanted, then. Why not smile, Anthony?
Why are your lips pursed like that? Come on, turn that frown upside down. Smile. Laugh. Do as I do.
Enough! Shut up!
Such terrifying eyes, brother. There's murder in them.
The eyes of a murderer! The eyes of a sinner!
Shut! Up!
Hahaha! We're waiting for you, Anthony. We'll see you in the flames of hell.
Is that so?
I'm already being burnt every day by the flames of revenge.
What do I care about the flames of hell, as long as I can tear you apart with my own two hands?
What does a charred corpse have to fear from the fire?
Then come find us, Anthony. Hahahaha.
I will. I'll step into the flames.
A fire burns in his eyes.
Argh—!
Argh...
It's that dream again... my head...
(Covers face) What time is it...?
Good morning, operator. It is currently 04:24. Current weather is overcast, and the temperature is 26 degrees.
Four in the morning... only three hours of sleep, then.
...Forget it, I can't get back to sleep.
My sheets are soaked with sweat.
I'll need to change them... the pillow, too.
You have a new message, operator.
Anthony, we found the money your dad left in Bunkerhill City. There's more than enough for us to make a comeback.
Are you still haunted by what happened to your parents?
It's not your fault. HydeBro carried out their entire plan while you were in Mansfield. By the time we heard the news, it was already too late.
The Hyde brothers are nothing if not thorough. It's a miracle that you're still alive.
We went to great lengths to get in touch with you. Their eyes and ears are everywhere.
Try to pull yourself together. We'll take back what belongs to us.
Control, Anthony... don't let violence overcome you... control...
(Trembles)
...Damn it.
Damn it!
He picks up a chair and throws it at the wall, shattering the dressing mirror mounted there.
He sees his face reflected in the shards, twisted in anger.
Then, the fury fades.
Control, Anthony.
Anger and sorrow have never solved anything.
Training Room
(Gazes into distance)
(Hm, he looks distracted...)
Snap out of it, big guy!
What?!
(She's fast... I might hurt her with a hard block. I'll just protect my head.)
Where do you think you're looking?
(Now she's aiming for my midsection!)
Too late. It's all too late.
Huh...?
No—shut up!
Ouch!
Oh no... I'm sorry, Shura. Are you alright?
So that's how it is, big guy... You've never really come at me with your full strength, have you?
We're in very different weight classes. I'm afraid you wouldn't be able to fight back.
Hmph! It wasn't that bad. Bring it on! Just... gimme a second to get up.
Ow ow ow!
Apologies, I should have been more careful. I'll take you to sickbay.
...Eh, these things happen in training.
You look distracted, though. What's the matter? Didn't get much sleep last night?
Yes... Maybe I was too absorbed in the book I was reading.
Well, nothing to worry about! Next time we're free, let's grab a few drinks together. That'll knock you right out, if you let 'em.
I'd rather not even think about drinking until we get you to a doctor.
How is she, Domma?
Asleep for now. We'll need to keep her a coupla days for observation, but it don't look too serious to me.
How'd she get hurt?
I accidentally injured her today.
What?
Don't look at me like that.
You ain't the type to lose control, though...
Don't look so surprised, Domma. You've seen me in prison.
Yeah, which is why I know just how hard you been tryin' to hide that side of you.
You look awful, Anthony.
...I've been having trouble sleeping. Seeing the same nightmare every night.
In it, I'm standing in a pool of blood, with blood on my hands, and the Hyde brothers are lying dead on the ground.
That's new, never had no dreams like that before. Somethin' happen?
Bad news from Bunkerhill City.
Your folks...
Educated guess?
Yeah, saw that letter on your desk when I was returnin' a book. Under a pile of books, but there ain't no hidin' those tear stains.
I've submitted my resignation and will be leaving in a few days. I've been here too long. It's time I faced it. Everything.
Figured this day'd come, sooner or later.
Sometimes, I can't help but think... what if you left all that behind and stayed here? Wouldn't that be swell?
I've considered it, Domma.
Once, I thought I would give up on revenge after I'd rescued my parents.
But now, my only desire is to repay blood with blood.
But you ain't never killed no one, Anthony.
How does it feel? How does it feel to take a life with your own hands?
Can you tell me, Domma? How did it feel when you injected poison into a prisoner's veins? How did it feel when you sent the body to the incinerator for disposal?
...It hurt, at first. You feel sick, can't sleep, start seein' stuff that ain't there.
Then, you try to justify it. Tell yourself they deserved it, that you did the right thing.
Then, one day, when enough people have stopped breathin' on account of you, you stop feelin' anything at all. You seen enough death.
That point, whatever crimes they did in life don't much matter no more. Their deaths don't neither.
Does it take a long time?
Yeah, long and painful. Had to keep remindin' myself it was just a job. But how 'bout you, Anthony?
How would you get through it?
Seems to me you made up your mind to face it without givin' a single thought to how.
We're goin' together, Anthony. I can help you.
No, this is my problem. I can't drag you into this.
I's already in it. I helped break you outta Mansfield, 'member?
That's enough, Domma, this is not open for discussion.
Anthony—
A-Anthony!
Are you awake, Shura?
I hearda you hadda bottle of fine whiskey... when will we getta have a taste of it?
How about next Wednesday? Ya free that day, and I'm free that day...
Huh? But you're injured. You shouldn't drink for a while.
Injured... ya, I'm injured, can't drink...
Why... *sob* I'm so sad... *sob*
(Is she ok?)
(Must be the anesthetic.)
(I see...)
Anthony...
Yes?
Promise me. Promise me you won't leave without sayin' goodbye.
...Alright.
Your exit papers are in order, sir. I'm sure you have plenty on your plate right now, so I took the liberty of bringing the paperwork over.
Sorry, and thank you. I should have come over to pick them up myself.
It's fine, I just happened to be passing through. Have a nice day, sir.
You too.
Well, that went quicker than I anticipated.
(Looks around)
I should clean up before I leave. Fortunately, there isn't much here.
These books... they can go to the library.
These bottles of liquor... I'll drop them off in the wine storage room.
...Oh, I almost forgot, the action movies I borrowed from Robin. I should remember to return them.
A leaf bookmark from Kafka, and this doll... As I recall, a Christmas present from Pinecone.
What's with all the trinkets in this drawer? I don't even remember putting them there. No doubt the kids staying at Medical will enjoy them, though.
Well, that's about it. Now to start packing... I should only need a few changes of clothes.
He freezes.
The suit hangs in the middle of the wardrobe, clear as day. He remembers everything about it, from picking the cloth, to getting measured, to the delivery.
Everyone could see how much he liked it. Everyone thought he would wear it at every opportunity.
In fact, he has hardly ever done so.
He did not want to blemish it.
You have a new message, operator.
Got your message, Anthony. We've made arrangements to get you to Bunkerhill City. We have people waiting for you at Tkaronto.
I look forward to seeing you. Your parents, my brother... we have so many scores to settle with the Hyde brothers.
He lifts a hand and touches a tiny piece of embroidery on the collar.
It is in the shape of a tower.
Eventually, reluctantly, his arm comes back down again.
What a fool I was... Why did I buy this, knowing that I would eventually leave?
Such a fool.
Dr. Silence. Is Domma here?
Sorry, Anthony, you might have to wait. She's treating a patient that came in this afternoon.
May I wait for her here?
Of course. Water?
No, thank you. I wouldn't want to get in your way.
Alright, I'll be making my rounds.
(Glances at watch)
I hope there's enough time...
Young man! Hey, young man!
Oh, sorry, were you speaking to me?
Yeah, for a while now, but seems like you didn't hear me.
I apologize; I was checking the time. Did you need something?
No, I just saw a hole in your shirt, so I was asking if you could come over so I could fix it.
Thank you. I suppose I didn't notice it because I was in a hurry.
But I'm afraid I have to leave soon.
Sit down already. Just because I'm old doesn't mean my hands don't work. It'll only take a few minutes.
...Thank you, ma'am.
You're a friend of Dr. Domma's?
Yes.
That's what I thought. You're always stopping by to see her.
Are you a patient of hers?
Yeah, she's really nice. I've got bad knees, and she's been a lot of help.
She's always been kind like that.
I guess you already know that she's leaving? She told me yesterday that I'm being handed over to Dr. Silence.
...Is that so. What a shame.
Must've heard some dumb patient calling her a weirdo behind her back. Silly, really! She's so patient and detailed. You don't get many doctors like her.
I completely agree.
But I guess that's that. Dr. Silence said she tried to convince her to stay, but she wouldn't change her mind.
She may be gentle on the surface, but she's stubborn. Once she puts her mind to something, no one can change it.
After relying on her for everything when I was stuck in a hospital bed, helping fix her friend's clothes is the least I could do.
There, how's that?
Wonderful. Thank you.
Oh, there's no need to thank me.
(Glances at watch)
Are you leaving?
Yes, I have to go.
You sure you don't want to wait? She'll be done in a minute.
No.
Hold on, you're going by yourself? I thought she was coming with you.
No, I came to say goodbye. I'm the only one who's leaving.
Oh, I must've misunderstood then. I could've sworn you were taking her with you.
No, it's better for her to stay at Rhodes Island. My revenge is my own business. I don't want to drag anyone else into it.
Speaking of which, can you do something for me, Dr. Silence?
Well, you can ask.
Can you give this book to her?
Just a book?
And a message. Tell her that...
Tell her I haven't finished it yet. Tell her to keep it safe.
When will you be back for it? What do I tell her?
Silence is the crueler answer, you know.
You take care. I need to go now.
Anthony!
Anthony...
...*sigh*.
Silence looks down and sees that the corner of one page has been folded. She opens the book and sees an illustration.
A man stands in a prison cell, his back to the window, his face obscured by shadows and iron bars. He extends a wilted finger through the bars and out beyond the picture.
There is a single line of text beneath the illustration.

lines.st: I have sinned. I have killed. I seek no sympathy, no forgiveness, no salvation. I seek only suffering, and eternal torment.
